Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social

Class SocialChainCustomizer

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social.SocialChainCustomizer
All Implemented Interfaces:
LoginChainCustomizer
public class SocialChainCustomizer extends Object implements LoginChainCustomizer
Customizes the login/UI chain with the sign-in with external providers: http.oauth2Login(...) with the client registrations of the configured providers, the user services that resolve the local account, the success handler that grants the federated factor and, for Apple, the signed client secret and the form post callback.

The endpoints of the framework (/oauth2/authorization/* starts a sign-in, /login/oauth2/code/* receives the provider's answer) are public. The login page is the server's own, so the provider's page is never chosen automatically even when one provider is configured. Apple posts its answer to the callback from another site, so that one callback is exempt from CSRF protection (the state of the authorization request protects it) and the session cookie must be sent on a cross-site post (see the documentation of the social login). The same endpoints serve the explicit link flow of the identities page: the success and failure handlers tell a link apart.
